name: r6b_tou_bank_lead_follows_primary__v4
description: A time-of-use peak starts at 16:15. The house is at 72 F and banking toward 68 F means 4 F of cooling. v3's learned rate is slow (1 F per hour); v4's fitted AC is a realistic 3.5 F per hour (3.1 F in the first hour through the house's hidden mass), and on a 90 F afternoon the house leaks heat back in at 0.05 of the gap per hour. Primary engine v4 (v3 is the live comparison engine): the lead comes from v4's OWN house model (thermal mass and a modest sun term included), stepped with the AC fully on against the forecast, not from a first-order formula (Issue #1517). That model needs about 135 minutes (155 with the 1.15 safety factor), so the bank window opens at 13:40, 40 minutes after this scenario starts and 155 minutes before the peak. The same house gives a different start under every other lead: v3's slow rate 12:15 (the 240-minute cap), the first-order leak formula on v4's rates 14:06, the plain delta/rate formula 14:36. Nothing is banked before 13:40, and the thermostat is told 68 F at the 13:44:59 check (the first 5-minute check at or after the window start), not at the 14:00 half-hour cycle.

events.note: The 13:30 plan cycle (the bank window has not started).
The 14:00 plan cycle (the bank window opened at 13:40 and is running).
End of run: three minutes after the 14:25 check.

assertions.reason: Before the window opens nothing is banked.
Until the window opens the thermostat is only told the comfort setpoint (the 13:00 setup and the 13:30 cycle).

The window the plan shows starts 155 minutes before the 16:15 peak, from v4's own house model: v3's rate would start at 12:15 (240-minute cap), the first-order leak lead at 14:06, the plain formula at 14:36, the 45-minute default at 15:30.
The thermostat is told 68 F at the first 5-minute check at or after the window start (13:44:59), with no comfort write before it, not at the 14:00 half-hour cycle.
The plan list names the same 13:40 start the thermostat acted on.

verdict.summary: The time-of-use bank opens by the primary engine (v4) house model, and the plan and the thermostat agree on when
verdict.observed_behavior: Window 13:40 (v4's house model needs about 135 min raw, 155 min with the 1.15 safety factor); nothing banked before it; first 68 F written at the 13:44:59 check, not at the 14:00 cycle.
verdict.expected_behavior: The AC is not run for hours more than the house needs before a peak price period, and the house is banked when the peak starts: the lead is v4's own house model (thermal mass, sun, leak), which sees what a first-order formula misses on a hot afternoon (Issue #1517). Re-derived 2026-11-11 with the owner's approval (third re-derivation for #1517): the inputs changed (hidden-mass coupling 0.6 to 0.3, sun 0.7 to 0.2) so that v4's stepped lead lands inside the run, below the 240-minute cap, and this golden tells the engines apart again. The earlier inputs put every lead at the cap, identical to the v3 twin, so a regression to v3's rate or to the first-order formula would have passed.

source: synthetic: Issue #1230 R6b (primary prediction engine drives decisions), redesigned per the independent review; DP-11 pending, unsigned
